To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number of arthroscopies is increasing, that the total knee replacement is the operation of choice, that the survival rate is improving, that complications are rare and that the unicompartmentar prostheses should be abandoned.

the total knee arthroplasy is the most successful prosthesis in rheumatoid arthritis and that the unicompartment arthroplasy, which is a less invasive operation, is not a better alternative in osteoarthrosis.

1) the total knee prosthesis has become the standard prosthesis in RA and is gaining popularity in OA; 2) the survival of total knee prosthesesis has improved in time, while the survival of the unicompamental prosthesis has not improved; 3) failed unicompamental prostheses should be replaced with total knee prosthesises; and 4) the risk of the most serious complications has decreased.

the epidemiology of knee arthroplastics, the design and quality of the prostheses and the complications.
the epidemiology of the arthroplastie surgery and its complications.
the development of knee arthroplasts in Sweden.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the knee arthroplastic techniques have improved and the survival rates are steadily increasing.
the total knee arthroplastics are a safe and reliable treatment for OA and RA and that the unicompartment prostheses are less safe and reliable, particularly in RA.
the Swedish knee register has been of great help to us in the development of knee arthroplastic surgery in Sweden.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the register has been able to identify the best prosthetic designs, to show the importance of the surgeon's training and to demonstrate the importance of a careful selection of the patients.

we have found the register to be a useful tool for the orthopaedic surgeon to monitor his own and his colleagues' results and for the patient to have an informed opinion of the results to be expected.
we have found that the total knee replacement has a high survivorship in RA and OA and that the unicompartmentar prosthesis is not as successful in RA as in OA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the register has been of great help to the Swedish orthopaedic surgeons in their decision-making and in their quality control.
the register has proved to be a valuable tool for the evaluation of prosthetic designs, surgical techniques and the development of new prostheses.
the Swedish Knee Arthroplasty Register provides a reliable source for information on the epidemiology and the results of knee arthroplasts in Sweden.
